title: Context and memory in an agent

items.stem: A student chats with your assistant on Monday about a CNC router job. On Thursday they start a new chat. You built no storage or loading code. What does the assistant know about Monday?

options.text: Nothing, because each new session starts with an empty context
A summary, because the model keeps one after each conversation
Everything, because the model stores all chats it has had
The key points, because the system prompt records each chat

items.stem: Your assistant's fixed context (system prompt plus tool descriptions) is 1,500 tokens. A request takes 3 model calls. The first call sends only the fixed context; each later call sends 1,000 more tokens than the call before it. How many input tokens are sent over the 3 calls in total?
Your 10-page set of makerspace rules is about 8,000 tokens in total. The assistant must answer questions from it. What is the most sensible first design?

options.text: Build a chunked embedding index and retrieve the top passages
Put all of it in the system prompt and skip retrieval entirely
Let the model recall the rules from what it learned in training
Save the rules as notes the model writes from its own chats

items.stem: In one sentence, why is a program-owned training record safer than a note the assistant writes itself for the fact "this student may use the band saw"?

A student asks, "Why is my print stringing?" The 3D printer manual says "filament oozes between parts; lower the nozzle temperature or enable retraction." The manual never uses the word "stringing". Which search is more likely to find this passage?

options.text: Embedding search, since it matches meaning and not exact words
Keyword search, since the question's words must appear in it
Neither one, since both need the exact word to find a page
Both equally, since search type does not affect what is found
